props.text: 12301 Wilshire Blvd, Suite 205 · Los Angeles, CA 90025
West LA Implants wants every patient to be able to read, navigate and book on this site, whatever tools they use to do it.
The site is designed to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at level AA, and is checked against them as it changes.
Some pages carry a third-party accessibility widget that adjusts type size, contrast and spacing. It is provided by the practice’s web partner and can be opened from its icon.
Every page has one heading that names it and a logical heading order beneath. Landmarks, lists and buttons are real HTML elements, so screen readers announce them correctly.
Every link on the site can be reached and activated with a keyboard, and the focus is always visible.

Type is sized in relative units and scales with your browser settings. Colour contrast between text and background meets the AA ratio, including the text that fills in as you scroll, which starts readable and only gets stronger.
Photographs carry descriptive alternative text. Decorative images are marked so they are skipped.
The site uses scroll-driven animation. If your system is set to reduce motion, every animation is disabled and every piece of content is shown in full, in place.
Films never autoplay with sound. Videos of patients are linked with descriptions.
Tell the practice and it will be fixed. And anything on this site can also be done by phone.

Keep biting on the gauze for 30 to 60 minutes. Do not spit, rinse, use a straw, smoke, or drink carbonated or alcoholic beverages for at least 24 hours. Empty your mouth passively. The goal is to keep the clot in the socket and avoid the painful complication known as dry socket.

Expect one or more of: minor pain, swelling, bruising, limited opening, pain in the jaw or ear, a sore throat. Listen to your body and take it easy. No heavy lifting, spitting, sucking, alcohol or smoking.
Brush gently. A lukewarm salt water rinse freshens the mouth, but do not spit; let it empty passively. The corners of the mouth may crack and dry; moisturise often.

Over-the-counter medication (ibuprofen, naproxen or acetaminophen) as directed on the bottle. Cold compresses in ten-minute intervals for the first 24 hours. Swelling usually starts to go down within 72 hours; call if it does not change.

Some oozing is normal for the first 12 to 24 hours; put a hand towel on your pillow. For heavier bleeding, apply firm pressure with one or two folded gauze pads or a damp tea bag for 30 to 60 minutes and keep your head elevated. Call if it does not subside.

Plenty of fluids, no carbonated or alcoholic drinks. Soft foods: yogurt, milkshakes without a straw, soups, fish, pasta. Nothing too spicy. Some tenderness when chewing and difficulty opening wide is normal.

Leave sutures alone; they are removed at a fifteen-minute visit in 7 to 10 days. Finish any antibiotics even if symptoms fade; some antibiotics reduce the effectiveness of birth control pills and other medications. Take any prescribed pain medication or rinse as directed.
Reduce activity. No running, weight lifting, strenuous aerobic activity or contact sports for 48 hours. Avoid exercises that put your head below your heart, such as Pilates or yoga.

Immediately after surgery, keep ice-cold water in your mouth or cold foods such as ice cream or low-fat yogurt for 6 to 8 hours, as continuously as possible, letting them defrost in the mouth to cool the surgical site. An external ice pack is of little value. Clean the teeth that did not have surgery as normal. Try not to play with the top covers over the implants.
Some discomfort is expected after any surgery. Take prescribed pain medication as directed, with milk and food if nausea develops. Do not drink alcohol with pain medication.

Anti-inflammatory medication is generally prescribed for 3 to 4 days. Cold liquids for 6 to 8 hours after surgery and for the rest of that day are essential; after 24 hours any temperature is fine. Do not apply heat for 72 hours.
A small amount is expected. No spitting, rinsing or sucking through a straw. Biting on the gauze provided, soaked in cold water, prevents bleeding.
Cold, soft, mainly liquid foods for 3 to 4 days; nothing hard, chewy, crunchy or spicy. Do not wear dentures for the first two weeks, or until the doctor says so.

After a sinus lift or augmentation
Reduce activity. No running, weight lifting, strenuous aerobic activity or contact sports for 48 hours; no exercises with the head below the heart. Do not take airplane flights for 10 days.
Care of your mouth and nose

Ice-cold water or cold foods in the mouth for 6 to 8 hours after surgery, as continuously as possible; a gentle external ice pack may help. Clean the teeth that did not have surgery. Try not to sneeze, cough hard or blow your nose; any of these can disturb the graft.

Prescribed pain medication as directed, with milk and food if nauseous, never with alcohol. Anti-inflammatories for 3 to 4 days. Cold liquids for the rest of the day of surgery; no heat for 72 hours. An external ice pack in cycles of 15 minutes on, 15 off.
A small amount is expected, and you may have nosebleeds. No spitting, rinsing or sucking; bite on the cold-soaked gauze provided. Do not blow your nose.
Cold, soft, mainly liquid foods for 3 to 4 days; nothing hard, chewy, crunchy or spicy. No dentures for the first two weeks, or until the doctor says so.

For congestion use a decongestant spray such as Afrin, but do not clear the nose by blowing; a cotton swab if needed. Saline spray keeps a dry nose moist. Finish antibiotics; call about any reaction. Do not smoke.

One solid block of zirconia, milled into a full arch and secured to your implants. It is the strongest material in dentistry and the closest match to the colour and translucency of teeth.
Traditional dentures and some hybrids set porcelain teeth into an acrylic base. Two materials, one weak seam, and a plastic that stains and wears.
A zirconia arch has no seam and no base. It is one piece, with the physical strength of titanium and the look of enamel.
Leaders in implant dentistry consider this the superior full-arch restoration. Here is what the material actually does.
The colour and translucency of enamel, custom shaded to your gums, lips and skin tone.
Everyday wear and strong bite forces without fracturing, for decades.

Planned digitally from your scan and milled to fit your implants and your face.

Secured to implants, the arch keeps the jawbone stimulated and healthy. It feels smooth against the gums and needs no adhesive, no soaking and no relines.
